predecessors.name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan
predecessors.text: East Pakistan: 'East Bengal was renamed East Pakistan in 1956 as part of the One Unit Scheme'; it came to Pakistan in the 'partition of Bengal between India and Pakistan by the Radcliffe Line' of 15…

ledger.x: 25 March 1971: Pakistan's army strikes East Pakistan.
December 1971: the seat of government moves from Meherpur to Dhaka.

wars.name: Bangladesh Liberation War
wars.outcome: 'Bangladeshi-Indian victory': Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 and East Pakistan became the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

wars.name: Chittagong Hill Tracts insurgency
wars.outcome: 'The Chittagong Hill Tracts region experienced unrest and an insurgency from 1975 to 1997'; a peace accord was signed in 1997 and the region 'remains militarised'.

certainty.note: The war: East Pakistan's land is held by Pakistan until 16 December 1971 and the borders of the new state are those of the old province.
The border with India follows the Radcliffe Line of 15 August 1947 ('the partition of Bengal between India and Pakistan by the Radcliffe Line'); the Myanmar border and the coast are fixed.
